purge-ok.section: The whole plan in five sentences
purge-ok.question: Are you comfortable with that split: throw away all derived data and rebuild it, keep the code and fix it?
purge-ok.selected: I want the code rebuilt from scratch too, whatever it costs
purge-ok.notes: And if you'd purge and re-import all of the data.

container-shape.question: How should a source that concerns several clients be stored?
container-shape.selected: One copy, tagged with every account it is about (recommended)

google-filing.question: When you name a Drive folder or Chat space as a source, how should its account be decided?
google-filing.selected: Match the name against the account list and ask you to confirm once (recommended)

visibility-states.question: Confirm the three sharing states.
visibility-states.selected: Private (owner only) · Agency · Agency + that client (recommended)

email-default.question: Your own Gmail and Calendar: what is the default when it comes in?
email-default.selected: Shared with the agency by default; I mark private ones
email-default.notes: For each source, we should be able to mark it. We should be able to control owner, shared with, and compartment. Also, when I go into the details, I should be able to see the number of pieces per source and which piece. I should be able to see the last modified timestamp too.

client-portal.question: Should clients get answers from the knowledge base in their portal, in this build?
client-portal.selected: No — agency only for now; design the fence so it can be added later (recommended)
client-portal.notes:
And when they do add sources into their own compartment, they become the owner, but they don't have an option to limit this information. Everything they share will go into, of course, their own account compartment or app compartment, however we're doing it. I think app compartment is better: account compartment and sub-compartment per app.

Whenever they upload anything there, in the future, when we build the ability for them to interact with the knowledge base, it builds up there. They can add things to their own compartment to that app, and whatever they upload is shared with them and the agency by default. They can't change that.

Of course, if we build this in the future, just make sure that we document that this is what we want to build, and we keep it open-ended so that we can build on this.

chk-visibility.question: Alaap’s own Gmail holds a thread with FluClinic about Stripe. He has not shared it. Aurora asks “what did FluClinic say about Stripe?” What happens?
chk-visibility.selected: Aurora’s answer cannot use it; if Alaap asks, his can
chk-visibility.notes: Yeah, of course this is true.

date-rule.question: Confirm the relevancy-date rule.
date-rule.selected: Frozen things (mail, chat, transcripts, events): when they happened. Living things (docs, sheets, records): last change (recommended)
date-rule.notes: Remember that we should have a compartment per account and then a sub-compartment per app. Just generally telling you.

context-line.question: Add the context line to every piece?
context-line.selected: Yes, written by the cheapest capable model (recommended)

records-as-cards.question: Turn app records (tickets, stories, tasks, accounts, contacts, sprints, processes) into find-only cards, read live when needed?

chk-widen.question: A 100-page PDF is 100 pieces. A question matches piece 47 only. What does the new system do before answering?
chk-widen.selected: Reads 46 and 48 as well, and tells the reader which document all of it is from

dedup-canonical.question: When one thing arrives several ways, which copy is the source of record?
dedup-canonical.selected: The richest text wins; the others are recorded as sightings and linked (recommended)

dedup-upload.question: You upload a PDF that is already in the library, byte for byte. What should happen?
dedup-upload.selected: Refused with a link to the existing one (recommended)

chat-grain.question: Google Chat: what is one piece?
chat-grain.selected: A run of consecutive messages from one thread, each stamped with speaker and time (recommended)
chat-grain.notes: Also, remember that compartments are happening per account and then per app as well. Also, what we'll see for many things, like emails and anything from Google, is that they have the capacity to be shared by multiple people. Alex, Aurora, and Alaap can share the same space with the knowledge base, but all of them are in the same space. That data: how do we make sure that there are not three duplicate sources? How does this work?

sheets.question: Spreadsheets: how should a sheet become pieces?
sheets.selected: Each sheet tab becomes one document of plain text

video.question: Loom, Tella and YouTube links uploaded from the app — get the transcript?
video.selected: Must-have now: YouTube captions + Loom/Tella transcript APIs, and Whisper on Workers AI for anything without one
video.notes: Only search for transcripts, no need to transcribe audio, so no need for Wispr.

live-google.question: During a question, should the system read Google live, or trust the index it refreshed within the last fifteen minutes?
live-google.selected: Trust the index; read app records live, never Google (recommended)
live-google.notes: Quick question: if we could also read Google Live, then what is the point of the knowledge base? Just curious, please answer this: if everything can just be read live, why even store everything in this vectorized format and index stuff?

sync-cadence.question: How fresh does Google material need to be?

chk-gate.question: Alaap uploads “FluClinic API guide.pdf”. Two weeks later Ishita uploads the identical file. What does the system say to Ishita?
chk-gate.selected: “Already in the library since [date] — here it is”

brain.question: Which model runs the planner, the re-read and the writing?
brain.selected: Stay on Cloudflare Workers AI only (Kimi / Llama) — under a cent; weaker planning and judgement; nothing leaves the platform

rerank-policy.question: The re-read step specifically (reading forty passages against the question): same policy as above, or its own?
rerank-policy.selected: Same brain as the loop — one policy, one place text goes (recommended)

latency.question: How long may a good answer take?
latency.selected: Up to a minute — thoroughness over speed
latency.notes: Anything under a minute or equal to a minute is great, as long as we can see how it's thinking, what happened, and the answers are brilliant.

show-thinking.question: Show the loop’s steps in the interface while it runs (“planning… searching 3 ways… re-reading 40… writing”)?
show-thinking.selected: Yes — it is honest and it makes waiting bearable (recommended)

fanout-cap.question: How many parallel searches and lookups may one question launch?
fanout-cap.selected: Up to 12 — dig as deep as it wants

structured-route.question: Confirm: counting, ranking and “across all clients” questions go to the record tools, never to the passages.

answer-language.question: Half your material is German. If the question is in German, the answer is…
answer-language.selected: Always in the asker’s app language setting

chk-route.question: Aurora asks “which client has the most open tickets?” Which path does the planner take?
chk-route.selected: Call the ticket tool for every client and count
chk-route.notes:
Ideally, this would be it. Also, I've been toying around with the idea for a master index. For example, when I ask it a question that involves pronouns, including an app, an account, or a stakeholder, there should just be one centralised index with the name and path to the correct table or database, depending on whether sharded or not sharded. I hope this makes sense.
Sometimes I can ask a question like, "Oh, is Paras from the flu clinic opening any new tickets? What was the average number of tickets opened in the last 7 days?" Now, because I mentioned flu clinic and I mentioned Paras, the first thing it can do is figure out:
- What is flu clinic?
- What is Paras?
- Is Paras a stakeholder?
- Is Paras an app?
- Is Paras an account?
- Is flu clinic an app?
- Is flu clinic an account?
One centralised index, I think, will help with that a lot. What do you say?

chk-refuse.question: Someone asks “what is the capital of France?” The reader receives the forty nearest passages, all about clients. What should it do?
chk-refuse.selected: Say the library holds nothing on this

bar-shape.question: Who makes the “we have nothing on that” call?
bar-shape.selected: The reader, after reading the shortlist; a low score only filters obvious nonsense first (recommended)

uncertain.question: The reader finds something relevant but thin. Should it…
uncertain.selected: Answer, and say plainly what is missing (recommended)

refusal-log.question: Log every refusal with what the shortlist held, so we can see false refusals within a day?

exam-failed.question: Write down real questions you have asked the knowledge base that gave a bad answer or a refusal. As many as you remember, one per line. These become the first rows of the exam.
exam-failed.notes:
- How does a chemist get reimbursed for a jab?
- What did we agree with Asekurans about the extraction transcript?
- What are the latest 10 to 15 rules on the HOGO HORST matching?
- What was the latest bug with flu clinic?
- What is happening with Paddlebase?
- How many days in advance can trainers book trainings?
- How many apps does Paddlebase have?
- How does the knowledge base work in the Kwapso system?

exam-authors.question: Who writes the rest of the exam?
exam-authors.selected: Let the agent draft them from the material and I approve

exam-modes.question: Which kinds of question must the exam cover? Tick all.
selected: Paraphrases — the same fact in different words
Questions we genuinely have nothing on (must refuse)

exam-gate.question: Rule: no ranking change ships unless the exam score does not drop. Agree?
exam-gate.selected: Yes — the exam is the gate (recommended)

budget.question: What monthly ceiling for the knowledge base’s AI spend would make you comfortable?

usage-guess.question: How many people will ask questions daily, six months from now?

chk-scale.question: The library grows from 10,000 pieces to 1,000,000. What happens to the cost of one question?

parallel.question: How many lanes can you run at once?
parallel.selected: Four or more — I have the usage for it

build-models.question: Confirm the model split for the build.
build-models.selected: Opus plans and reviews; Sonnet builds every lane (recommended)

timeline.question: Which do you want?
timeline.selected: Everything in one push, however long it takes

cut-order.question: If it slips, what must survive the cut? Tick everything that ships no matter what.
selected: The bar becomes a judgement, not a number
Pieces carry the full identity card and context line
The answer loop with a real reader

staging-rule.question: Nothing reaches production until the new exam passes on staging and you have asked it your own ten questions. Agree?

laws.question: Some of this touches the machine-checked laws (R23 cited answers, R26 the fence, R47 assistant coverage). Each change must go through the seam the law guards and add a rot-checked entry where one is needed. Confirm the lanes are told this, and that a lane which cannot satisfy a law stops and reports rather than working around it.

worries.question: What worries you most about this build? Tick all.
selected: It burns my usage and does not finish
It finishes and the answers are still mediocre
The agents change more than they were asked to
The exam gets written to pass rather than to test

missing.question: What is missing entirely — something you expected to be asked and were not?
missing.selected: I have written it in the notes
missing.notes:
Well, there's a lot to think about.
1. The index of all proper nouns or available items.
2. Compartmentalization of accounts and then sub-compartmentalization of apps per account, because there are some accounts with three or four apps, so that could get confusing if it's not segregated, right?
Of course, it can pull from all apps simultaneously, right, because there are many systems that we build that consist of one or two apps that work together. It just knows that this is from this app, this is from this app, and it can read both and answer how the two apps work together.
Now I also want to get a breakdown of this: how we get the material and collection, splitting into pieces, turning meaning into numbers. How are we getting the right answer out?
- Searching twice at once
- Rereading the shortlist
- Deciding honestly
- Grounding
How do we answer with receipts? How do we send the odd ones elsewhere? How do we mark the homework?
Also, everything that was broken:
- Collection
- Splitting into pieces
- Searching twice
- Rereading the shortlist
- Deciding honestly
- Sending the odd ones elsewhere when marking the homework
How do we plan to fix this? You're going to test it with all these new questions, right? Also, at what point does Cloudflare have a scaling problem in terms of its vectorize and all of that?
Apart from that, nothing. I just want to now clear the card. Explanation: I want to know exactly what it is that we have now done, all of this research and found out, that we need to do that wasn't there before. If we do everything that we say we're going to do, how close are we to actually building an enterprise-grade knowledge base tool?
